why: The performance suite: one answer to 'how good is our performance' across the scenes players produce, in both engine profiles. Every scenario is a fixed plan (fixed inputs at fixed ticks, the production stepping order); scripts/perf/suite.py runs it under the exclusive GPU lock and scores it. Correctness is scripts/verify/correctness.sh, not this.
headline: high
score: geometric mean over scenarios of p95 step time / baseline p95 (replays: median evaluation time / baseline)

town.what: Vibe Town as the native app fields it (native-mac.sh --scene town): its 22 cars at the builder's parking spots, 16 stress iterations (the town qualification cap)

lab-truck.what: The vehicle lab's framed-house trial: the monster truck floored from 50 m out into the brick-veneer house (structures/vehicle-lab trials.mjs), the fleet's 64 stress iterations

lab-cannonball.what: The vehicle lab's cannonball-framed-house trial: the game's cannonball into the brick-veneer house, the truck parked on the rest pad

lab-meteor.what: The vehicle lab's meteor-framed-house trial: the game's meteor into the brick-veneer house, the truck parked on the rest pad

calib-demolition.what: Calibration scenario demolition (structures/calibration): three RC frames side by side, two blown down by charge sequences (east-first, core-first) and one left standing

phases.why: Vibe Town at rest with its parked fleet: the fixed cost every tick of a match pays
the eight cars parked along Main Street driven down it at once (destructible vehicles under load, the fleet's suspension and road contacts)
cannonballs and meteors into houses and the cinema, 1/3 s apart: fracture, correction passes, debris
a 4 t monster truck floored into a brick-veneer timber-frame house (impact about 3 s in)
the game's cannonball into the brick-veneer house
the game's meteor into the brick-veneer house
two three-storey RC frames brought down by their charges (firings at 1.0-1.9 s), the third standing: a large collapse and its debris
